We have the function 

$$
y=({x}^{2}+1)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{x}.
$$

First, we find the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product rule for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+1)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\cdot (2x)+(x)^{′}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+x{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x))}^{′} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+x\operatorname{cot}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+x\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=({x}^{2}+1)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =({x}^{2}+1)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{x}(\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+1}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+x\operatorname{cot}⁡x) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{x}(2x+({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+x({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cot}⁡x) \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{x}(({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+2x+x({x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$
